topic.title: Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal?

title: Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal?
description:
Why is a whole country wrapped inside another one?
The Gambia is one river, its banks, and a border drawn by two empires.
Sources: Britannica, Wikipedia (Nov 2026).
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Which border should we explain next? Comment

lines.text: Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal, like a worm inside an apple?
Gambia is a real country, with its own flag and its own money, and Senegal wraps around it on every side but the sea.
From the coast, it runs almost 480 km inland, yet at its widest it is only about 50 km across.
Senegal is its only neighbour, and their border winds on for 749 km, through villages, farms and forest.
So how did that happen? The answer is the river. In the age of sailing ships, it was a highway deep into Africa, and Britain held its mouth.
France held the land all around it, the colony that became Senegal.
So in 1889, the two empires made a deal. Britain kept the river, and land about 10 km back from its banks.
France took everything else. In 1965, Gambia became independent, inside exactly the same line.
So did anyone ever fix it? In 1982, the two countries even joined as one, Senegambia. By 1989, they had split again.
So a line drawn for river boats, about 10 km from the water, is still where a whole country begins and ends.
